topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the module structure, personal background, and key learning outcomes regarding cancer causation and carcinogen evaluation.

topics.label: Cancer etiology, intrinsic risk, and environmental epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer arises from an interplay between intrinsic genetic mutations and environmental exposures, evaluating population-level epidemiological patterns and the bad-luck hypothesis.

topics.label: Oncogenic pathogens and viral carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the mechanisms by which infectious agents, particularly Epstein-Barr virus in Burkitt lymphoma, contribute to malignant transformation.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how physical radiation and chemical carcinogens undergo metabolic processing to form DNA adducts and induce genetic damage.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, microenvironmental factors, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, including two-stage tumor promotion, tissue-specific timing, and host physiological susceptibility.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying, testing, and assessing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro approaches used to identify carcinogens and evaluate their associated health risks.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and summary
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by summarizing the core takeaways on environmental carcinogenicity and risk assessment.
